name: Lienzer Dolomiten
kurzbeschreibung: The Lienzer Dolomiten soar up to 2,770 m: bold rock spires, Karlsbader Hütte at Lake Laserzsee, Dolomitenhütte, and climbing paradise.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Lienzer Dolomiten are a breathtaking, heavily cragged mountain group of the Gailtal Alps rising immediately south of the Lienz valley basin in East Tyrol. The massif's highest peak is the Große Sandspitze at an altitude of 2,770 metres. With their sheer limestone and dolomite cliffs, daring rock needles, and deep glacial cirques, the Lienzer Dolomiten represent an internationally renowned paradise for mountaineers, climbers, and ambitious alpine hikers – crowned by legendary mountain huts such as the Dolomitenhütte and the Karlsbader Hütte.

Alpine History & Hiking Highlights

The mountaineering exploration began in the latter half of the 19th century when daring pioneers achieved first ascents of Sandspitze, Laserzkopf (2,718 m), and Spitzkofel (2,717 m). Today, a toll-paying panoramic mountain road winds from Lavant or Amlach up to the Dolomitenhütte (1,618 m), dramatically perched atop a rocky promontory. From here, a popular, scenic trail (approx. 2 hours walking time) ascends through the Laserztal valley to the Karlsbader Hütte at 2,260 metres. This traditional Alpine Club hut hugs the shores of the emerald-green Laserzsee, which mirrors the sheer walls of the Laserzwand. For climbing enthusiasts, the range offers over 100 alpine climbing routes, several demanding via ferratas (including the Laserz-Klettersteig, difficulty C/D), and a climbing park at the Dolomitenhütte. Multi-day trekkers also prize the high-altitude Dolomiten-Höhenweg.

Visit & Arrival

The hiking trails and via ferratas of the Lienzer Dolomiten are generally open during the summer season from mid-June to early October; both Karlsbader Hütte and Dolomitenhütte provide hospitality daily during these months. The toll road to the Dolomitenhütte is accessible seasonally (toll approx. €10.00 per car). Arrival by car: From Lienz via Amlach or Tristach, follow signs to Dolomitenhütte; a large hikers' car park is situated directly by the hut. By public transport: Rail (ÖBB) to Lienz station, from where the seasonal Lienzer Dolomiten Hikers' Bus runs on summer weekends and holidays directly to the Dolomitenhütte.

Tips

Sturdy, ankle-high mountaineering boots, surefootedness, and rain protection are essential for the ascent to Karlsbader Hütte and alpine routes; via ferratas require full via ferrata equipment with helmet. The sun terrace of the Dolomitenhütte offers a sensational plunging view and is also accessible to casual visitors directly by car or bus.
